signals.title: USD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Rate Differential
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.87, testing below the SMA20 at 156.89 while holding under the SMA50 at 159.14. The 25d risk reversal sits at −2.08, showing a strong put skew as the options market prices hedging protection. The G10 strength scorecard confirms USD as the week's leader at +1.426% across 9 pairs against JPY as the laggard at −1.127% across 7 pairs, producing a 2.553% bilateral spread. The OIS carry differential of +264bp favoring USD from SOFR at 3.62% versus TONA at 0.98% underpins the divergence despite the Bank of Japan lifting rates to 1.25%. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry advantage and scorecard outperformance sustain the structural bid. Catalyst: US Fed Industrial Production m/m at 13:15 UTC. Risk: Fed rate path reprices dovish and narrows the 264bp OIS spread, compressing the bilateral spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning + Volatility + Technical Anchor
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3348, sitting below the SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.3532, 1.3482, and 1.3455. CFTC leveraged funds net long stands at +40,361 contracts in the 86th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of +1.02, reflecting a crowded long positioning base alongside a −7,143 weekly reduction. Implied volatility runs at 5.0% against an HV30 of 4.1%, producing a +0.9% volume risk premium that shows options pricing moderate protection above realized movement. The OIS carry spread shows an 11bp differential favoring GBP from SONIA at 3.73% versus SOFR at 3.62%, though the Bank of England holding Bank Rate at 3.75% leaves the real rate at +0.35% under a mildly restrictive setting. Trade bias: Short GBP/USD; crowded spec longs unwinding against moving-average resistance. Catalyst: US Fed Industrial Production m/m at 13:15 UTC. Risk: Speculative positioning resumes net additions and breaks the pair back above the SMA200 cluster at 1.3455.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Options Complacency + Valuation Extreme

The BEER model fair value z-score stands at +1.95σ, marking the pair as rich relative to rate differentials and risk sentiment. CFTC leveraged funds report a net short of −13,968 contracts at the 12th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of −1.09. Trade bias: Long USD/CHF; trend persistence despite option complacency and rich valuation. Catalyst: SNB policy meeting on 24 Sep. Risk: Valuation mean-reversion triggers a sharp correction toward the SMA50 level at 0.8105.
